_comment: Themis exam AP policy for the Kali/Linux host. See docs/LINUX_AP.md. 'airgap' is the only profile that can prove no online lookup, no cloud AI, and no VPN or Tor -- because with no uplink there is nothing for any of them to reach.
_security_comment: wpa2 | wpa2+wpa3 | wpa3.  'wpa2+wpa3' (transition) is the default: WPA3 clients get SAE, which means a per-session key and no offline dictionary attack, while older laptops can still join with WPA2. 'wpa3' is strongest but refuses any client without SAE, which at 19 unknown laptops risks excluding a student on exam day -- find out at the dress rehearsal, not on the day.
_pmf_comment: 802.11w management-frame protection. 0=off 1=optional 2=required. Without it, deauthentication frames are unauthenticated and ANY student can knock classmates off the exam network, which then looks exactly like a genuine drop in the proctor console. 1 protects every client that supports it while still admitting those that do not; 2 protects everyone but refuses the rest.
_channel_comment: mt7921u does NOT support DFS channels in AP mode. Stay on 36-48 or 149-165 (US). 36 with 80MHz width covers 36-48.
_allowlist_comment: Profile 'allowlist' only, and it needs TWO lists because the two layers filter different things: dnsmasq filters NAMES, nftables filters ADDRESSES. Keeping them in agreement is manual and goes stale whenever the CDN rotates -- which is the clearest argument for profile 'airgap' or a validating CONNECT proxy instead. See docs/THREAT_MODEL.md.

enterprise._comment: Tier 2 identity -- see docs/IDENTITY.md. Not enabled for the first run.

radios._comment: every device ever made can see 2.4 GHz -- this is the inclusive one
5 GHz: faster and far less contended, for anything that can see it

_radios_comment: One adapter beacons on one channel, so dual-band is two radios -- which is all a dual-band router is. Both carry the SAME ssid and passphrase and are bridged, so a student sees ONE network and their device picks the band. ap_interface below stays as the single-radio fallback and is ignored while 'radios' is set.
_max_stations_comment: Per-BSS station limit, so with two radios it applies to EACH band separately. Set far above any possible roster: hitting it is not a visible failure, it is hostapd replying 'unable to handle additional associated stations' and the laptop showing a generic 'cannot connect' -- indistinguishable from a student who never turned up. A laptop resuming from sleep can also hold a second station entry until the old one ages out, so the effective ceiling is lower than the number.
